question: Which of the following was the capital of Vatsa Mahajanapada?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kausambi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vatsa Mahajanapada was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas in ancient India, mentioned in Buddhist and Jain texts.
 
• Kausambi was the capital city of Vatsa, situated near the modern-day location of Kosam on the Yamuna River in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The city was a significant center for trade and governance during the Mahajanapada period.
 
• Kausambi was renowned for its prosperity and served as a hub for economic activities and cultural exchanges.
 
• Udayana, a famous ruler of Vatsa, ruled from Kausambi and is known for his association with early Buddhist traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahajanapadas:** These were sixteen great kingdoms or oligarchic republics that existed in ancient India during the 6th century BCE.
 
• **Location of Vatsa:** Vatsa was situated in the central region of present-day Uttar Pradesh, near the Yamuna River.
 
• **Significance of Kausambi:** The city was fortified and developed as a major urban center with excellent infrastructure and trade networks.
 
• **Udayana:** He was a prominent king of Vatsa who played a key role in promoting Buddhism and was mentioned in several Buddhist texts.
 
• **Trade and Cultural Exchange:** Kausambi was an important node for trade routes, facilitating interactions between different regions of ancient India.
